item.title: 15 November 2026: The commission report on regulating therapy, Child Focused Courts, and the coordinated management of meaning (backup voices)
item.description:
Covers 2 to 15 November 2026, plus a few late-October items not covered before. The 8 November episode never reached the feed because of a publishing problem, so this one covers the fortnight. Recorded with backup (Kokoro) voices because the usual text-to-speech credits had run out. Papers were discussed from abstracts only; full texts not read.

Items

  • Profession news (commission report, launched 2 Nov): Unlocking Potential, Transforming Lives, from the Commission for the Future of Counselling and Psychotherapy (set up by the PCPB, which includes UKCP and BACP). Calls for steps towards statutory regulation, a review of volunteering and reporting on placements; NHS workforce table lists 386 WTE family and systemic psychotherapists (about 1%). PCPB, BACP response. Also: the Institute of Family Therapy merged with Family Action from 1 October (IFT).
  • Policy (MoJ policy papers, 28 Oct): Child Focused Courts, replacing the Child Arrangements Programme for private law cases, to cover all areas by March 2029; management information shows direct engagement with children in 82% (Cafcass) and 87% (Cafcass Cymru) of cases, against 30-37% before; many domestic abuse referrals are first-time disclosures. Delivery update, Target operating model
  • Policy (ministerial speech, 11 Nov): Josh MacAlister on the expansion of Family Group Decision Making and Family Network Support Packages, and shifting spending "into family systems". gov.uk. Brief: Alison McGovern says a new mental health strategy is due soon (speech, 9 Nov); children looked after statistics due 19 Nov.
  • Practice and theory paper: team treatment reviews when eating-disorder-focused family therapy feels stuck (Baudinet and colleagues, Maudsley). A proposal, not an evaluation. ANZJFT, online 8 Nov. Paired with a case study of peer-supported Open Dialogue becoming treatment as usual in an adult eating disorder service in Wales (ANZJFT, online 1 Nov).
  • Qualitative study (7 specialised family therapists, Belgium): adaptations in pace, style, contextualisation and setting when autism is suspected in a family. Therapist view only. Journal of Family Therapy, online 5 Nov
  • Practice-based study (15 trainee therapists, 86 clients, 1,035 session ratings, one US training clinic): "client-low" sessions, where the client rated the session low and the therapist did not (18.5%), were followed by worse client-reported functioning and symptoms; "all-low" sessions were not. Observational. JMFT, online 2 Nov
  • Brief mentions: RCT of the Attachment Video-feedback Intervention in French child protection services, 55 parents and 67 children (CCPP, online 5 Nov); RCT of group Parental Vigilant Care for 264 parents of adolescents on probation in Israel, lower dropout and gains in parental knowledge and anchoring at 2 months (J Fam Psychol, online 5 Nov); Dulwich Centre free course, Sparkling Moments from Michael White's Archive (Dulwich Centre).
  • Diary: 20 Nov, Reenee Singh on intercultural relationships (AFSP); 20 Nov, UKCP CFCSP AGM and Hugh Palmer CPD (AFSP); 26 Nov, EFTA Research Café on SysDok (EFTA); 30 Nov, older people and systemic practice (AFSP); 15 Dec, Barbara McKay on supervision and CMM (AFSP).

Concept corner: the coordinated management of meaning (CMM). Further reading: Pearce and Cronen (1980), Communication, Action and Meaning: The Creation of Social Realities; Pearce (2007), Making Social Worlds: A Communication Perspective; Cronen, Johnson and Lannamann (1982), Paradoxes, double binds, and reflexive loops, Family Process 21.

From the training room: asking families for session feedback, properly.

Unchecked this week: full texts of all papers (Wiley, SAGE and Springer blocked); Community Care (feeds broken); Nuffield Family Justice Observatory and NICE guidance lists (403); Cafcass news; NHS England psychological professions pages; KCC Foundation (site unreachable); Family Action's merger page (403); Taos Institute; The Psychologist; Therapy Today November contents; UKCP news (may be incomplete); Scottish and Welsh government news; Context issue 207 (contents only).

AI-generated summary; check the sources before relying on them in practice.

item.title: 1 November 2026: The Great EFT Schism, family interactions at clinical high risk for psychosis, and approach-method-technique
item.description:
Covers 18 October to 1 November 2026. All papers were discussed from abstracts and record metadata only; full texts not read.

Items

  • Cross-sectional survey, non-clinical community sample (545 couples): attachment-only versus multi-motivational (attachment, regard, attraction) accounts of couple satisfaction in emotion-focused couple therapy theory. Family Process, December 2026 issue
  • Observational and self-report study, 162 youths at clinical high risk for psychosis and their parents: family communication and symptoms. Journal of Family Psychology, online 19 Oct
  • Qualitative interview study (9 adolescents, 11 caregivers, one US emergency department): Black adolescents presenting with suicide risk and their caregivers, experiences of and barriers to mental health care. Child and Adolescent Mental Health, online 20 Oct
  • Profession news: AFSP is recruiting a CEO, closing Monday 2 November (AFSP); AFSP events listing, including the 10 November webinar on supervising high-conflict families (AFSP events).
  • Brief mention, scale development (mixed methods): Filial Caregiving Burnout in the Chinese cultural context. Family Process

Concept corner: Burnham's approach, method and technique. Further reading: Burnham (1992), Approach-method-technique: making distinctions and creating connections, Human Systems 3 (check the reference); Burnham's writing on relational reflexivity in Flaskas, Mason and Perlesz (eds), The Space Between (2005).

From the training room: presenting a family to your supervision group.

Unchecked this week: Journal of Family Therapy early view, Journal of Marital and Family Therapy full contents, Context magazine, Therapy Today, The Psychologist, Psychotherapy Networker, EFTA, Tavistock and Portman, Institute of Family Therapy, Anna Freud Centre, KCC Foundation, UKCP, NICE, NHS England and Children's Commissioner (web searches found nothing new for the week; nothing opened directly). The AFSP news page redirected and was not read. Journals were swept via PubMed only.

AI-generated summary; check the sources before relying on them in practice.

item.title: 25 October 2026: Care Together in Greater Manchester, Bluey and Bowen, and structural family therapy
item.description:
Covers 11 to 25 October 2026. Papers were discussed from abstracts and record metadata only; full texts not read.

Items

  • Policy (government press release, no evaluation yet): Care Together, a mental health pilot for children supported by social care, run by NHS Greater Manchester ICB with Stockport, Tameside and Rochdale; up to 9.4 million pounds over three years; names family therapy. DHSC and NHS England, 23 Oct
  • Policy briefs: Steps to Safety, GP-based domestic abuse referral service in 12 ICB areas (DHSC, 23 Oct); a tabled Social Housing Bill measure on tenancies for domestic abuse survivors (MHCLG, 20 Oct); children looked after statistics due 19 Nov.
  • Profession news: AFSP (the Association for Family and Systemic Psychotherapy, formerly AFT) is recruiting a CEO, closing 2 Nov (AFSP); annual conference, Glasgow, 15-16 Oct (AFSP); events including 27 Oct racism webinar, 24 Nov Newcastle, IFTA 2027 call; Context open call for writers.
  • Qualitative content analysis: Bluey read through Bowen family systems theory. ANZJFT, online 12 Oct
  • Mixed-methods feasibility pilot (three couples): Relational Suicide Intervention. Family Process, online 18 Oct
  • Practice report (no outcome data): the Métissages Group, a transcultural setting in France. Clinical Child Psychology and Psychiatry, online 21 Oct
  • Brief mentions: Parenting-STAIR adaptation for military-connected mothers (Family Process); chatbot answers to parent questions on child OCD (CCPP).

Concept corner: structural family therapy. Further reading: Minuchin (1974), Families and Family Therapy; Minuchin and Fishman (1981), Family Therapy Techniques.

From the training room: preparing for live supervision.

Unchecked this week: Journal of Family Therapy early view, Journal of Marital and Family Therapy (no day-level dates), Context magazine issues, Therapy Today, The Psychologist, Psychotherapy Networker, EFTA, Tavistock and Portman, Institute of Family Therapy, Anna Freud Centre, KCC Foundation, UKCP news, NICE, NHS England, Children's Commissioner. The AFT-to-AFSP rename comes from a search snippet.

item.title: 18 October 2026: A proposed family-enhanced CBT-E, a psychosis carers trial protocol, and externalising
item.description:
Covers 11 to 18 October 2026. A quiet week for new research, so the episode is shorter than usual. Both research items were discussed from abstracts only.

Items

  • Narrative review and conceptual proposal (no patient data): integrating family-based treatment components into CBT-E for adolescent eating disorders, as "Family-Enhanced CBT-E". The authors state it does not change the first-line status of family therapy and needs open and randomised trials. International Journal of Eating Disorders, online 14 Oct
  • Trial protocol (no results): stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial in six French first-episode psychosis centres of a nurse-led caregiver pathway (single-family and multifamily psychoeducation); primary outcome caregiver burden at six months. Registered NCT07041463. International Journal of Mental Health Nursing, online 12 Oct
  • Brief mention (title only): validation of the Couple Flourishing Measure in a Spanish population. Family Process. Diary: AFSP/AFT online webinar on racism in psychotherapy and supervision, 27 October. AFT events

Concept corner: externalising (narrative therapy). Further reading: White and Epston (1990), Narrative Means to Therapeutic Ends; Morgan (2000), What Is Narrative Therapy?; Maisel, Epston and Borden (2004), Biting the Hand That Starves You.

From the training room: the self of the therapist, with a three-line reflection after a session.

Unchecked this week: journals were swept via PubMed only (Journal of Family Therapy early view page not opened); NICE, NHS England, Children's Commissioner, Tavistock and Portman, Institute of Family Therapy, Anna Freud Centre and Context magazine found nothing new but were not checked directly. Full texts not read.

item.title: 13 October 2026: ODDESSI correspondence, carers in family-based treatment, and the Social GRRRAAACCEEESSS
item.description:
Covers 6 to 13 October 2026. A quiet week for new research. All items were discussed from abstracts or titles only.

Items

  • Three letters in Lancet Psychiatry (8 October), all titled "Open Dialogue: challenges in interpreting the ODDESSI trial results" (Morriss; Palanci; Hutton and Howard). Their content could not be opened, so it is not summarised; the episode only recaps the trial's null primary outcome. Morriss letter, Hutton and Howard letter, Palanci letter
  • Qualitative study (12 caregivers, New Zealand) of experiences of family-based treatment for adolescent anorexia: themes of an under-resourced system, an isolating treatment with limited guidance, and lasting psychological toll. Traumatic stress not formally assessed. International Journal of Eating Disorders, online 12 Oct
  • Recent context (23 September): therapist self-report of systemic techniques, 18 therapists and 165 recorded sessions in one New York clinic; self-report reliable overall but overestimated in individual sessions. Frontiers in Psychology
  • Brief mention: daily-diary network study of 43 mother-child dyads in Germany. Family Process. Diary: AFT conference, Glasgow, 15-16 October. AFT events

Concept corner: the Social GRRRAAACCEEESSS. Further reading: Burnham (2012), Developments in Social GRRRAAACCEEESSS: visible-invisible and voiced-unvoiced, in Krause (ed.), Mutual Intercultural Perspectives; Roper-Hall's work on the framework in systemic training.

From the training room: the first session with a family who do not want to be there.

Unchecked this week: Journal of Family Therapy (nothing found); the Lancet Psychiatry letters (blocked); JAACAP, JAMA Psychiatry, BMJ; NICE, NHS England, Children's Commissioner, Tavistock and Portman, Institute of Family Therapy, Context magazine; policy news. Full texts not read.

item.title: 12 October 2026: Carers and expressive writing, and the genogram
item.description:
Covers 5 to 12 October 2026. A quiet week, so a shorter episode. All three papers were discussed from abstracts only.

Items

  • Meta-analysis of expressive writing for family caregivers: 13 studies, mostly high risk of bias; small short-term effect on anxiety only (SMD -0.22, p = 0.041), nothing clear for depression, stress or burden. Family Process, online 9 Oct
  • Qualitative (transcendental-phenomenological) study of 9 young adult couples (18 people) living with sickle cell disease: six themes on shared and individual meaning. Contemporary Family Therapy, online 9 Oct
  • Single qualitative case study of structural-strategic therapy with an emerging adult with depressive symptoms and his family; illustrative, not evidence of effectiveness. ANZ Journal of Family Therapy, online 8 Oct
  • Diary: AFT conference, Glasgow, 15-16 October. AFT events

Concept corner: the genogram. Further reading: McGoldrick, Gerson and Petry, Genograms: Assessment and Intervention; Bowen, Family Therapy in Clinical Practice.

From the training room: keeping a reflective log, and reflection versus reflexivity.

Unchecked this week: Journal of Family Therapy and Child and Adolescent Mental Health (no results from database check); Lancet Psychiatry; NICE, NHS England, Children's Commissioner, Tavistock and Portman, Institute of Family Therapy, Context magazine; policy news. Full texts not read.

item.title: 9 October 2026: The Fonagy review, and reflecting teams (backup voices)
item.description:
Covers 2 to 9 October 2026. A thin week for family therapy research. Recorded with backup (Kokoro) voices because the usual text-to-speech credits had run out.

Items

  • Fonagy review of mental health conditions, ADHD and autism, published 9 October: the government says it argues for a needs-led system in which diagnosis is not the only route to support. Based on the government press release only; the full review was not read. gov.uk
  • Factorial randomised trial of three single-session online parent components for child anxiety: primary outcome null; the empathetic-responding component looked most promising on later secondary time points. Abstract only; sample size not confirmed. JAACAP, online 8 Oct
  • Mixed-methods study of digital disconnection and family emotional distance in 462 Vietnamese young adults plus 30 interviews. Cross-sectional; abstract only. ANZ Journal of Family Therapy, online 8 Oct
  • Qualitative interviews with 43 members of 11 families about misattributed parentage discoveries. Abstract only. Family Process, online 8 Oct

Concept corner: reflecting teams. Further reading: Andersen (1987), The reflecting team: dialogue and meta-dialogue in clinical work, Family Process 26; Andersen (1991), The Reflecting Team: Dialogues and Dialogues about the Dialogues.

From the training room: preparing for live supervision.

Unchecked this week: the full Fonagy review; JAACAP site (blocked); Journal of Family Therapy and Child and Adolescent Mental Health (nothing new found); BMJ only partly screened; NHS England, Tavistock and Portman, Institute of Family Therapy, Context magazine; an ACT premarital programme paper in Contemporary Family Therapy (title only).

item.title: 7 October 2026: Open Dialogue's ODDESSI trial, and circular questioning
item.description:
Covers 30 September to 7 October 2026. A quiet week for new family therapy research, so Hannah and Ben spend longer on the ODDESSI trial of Open Dialogue (published online in late August, in the October print issue, so context rather than news) and on a concept corner on circular questioning.

Items

  • ODDESSI, Open Dialogue versus treatment as usual, cluster-randomised trial, 494 adults in crisis: no difference in time to first relapse; lower inpatient admission and better self-rated recovery and satisfaction as secondary outcomes. Lancet Psychiatry 2026;13(10):841-851. Discussed from the abstract and press coverage; full text not read.
  • Parallel parent-child mindfulness RCT with 116 migrant dyads in Hong Kong: benefits mostly for parents, little for children. Family Process, online 2 Oct. Abstract only.
  • Conversation analysis of how therapists open collaborative-dialogic meetings (10 meetings, Western Sydney). Contemporary Family Therapy, online 1 Oct. Qualitative, very small corpus.
  • Growing Up in the 2020s first-year findings: a quarter of Year 8 pupils in England with a probable mental health condition. Anna Freud, 1 Oct. Also, as context, the Future Minds report card, 28 Sep.
  • Diary: AFT conference, Glasgow, 15-16 October.

Concept corner: circular questioning. Further reading: Cecchin (1987), Hypothesizing, circularity, and neutrality revisited: an invitation to curiosity, Family Process 26; Tomm (1987-1988), Interventive interviewing, Family Process.

From the training room: the first session with a family who do not want to be there.

Unchecked this week: publisher sites for Journal of Family Therapy and ANZ Journal of Family Therapy (database checks found nothing); Lancet page (blocked); AFT news and Context, NICE in-development pages, NHS England, Children's Commissioner, Tavistock and Portman, Institute of Family Therapy; domestic abuse, neurodiversity and workforce policy; the two ODDESSI commentaries were not read.
